findings.statement: A smaller index makes a bulk load faster
findings.detail: varint index 1088785 ops/s against flat 1050114 (varint vs flat: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 1.037, p=0.0601) -- within noise, not a result), with the file at 52.8 MB against 84.4 and the checkpoint at 0.172s against 0.243s, of which fsync is 0.068s against 0.094s. This is f31's flush half tested directly: if the bytes the index adds are what the checkpoint is paying for, removing 73.5% of them has to show here

findings.statement: The flat index reads faster than the varint one it replaced
findings.detail: flat 2203493 reads/s against varint 2285427 (flat vs varint: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 0.964, p=0.3785) -- within noise, not a result). This is the side a smaller index costs, and it is why F11.4 accepts +73.5% on the file deliberately: a section read in place cannot be compressed, and a compressed one is copied into every reader's heap

notes: both arms interleaved; the only difference is Options::flat_index
keys arrive in order, the shape EXT.13 finds Supdb behind on
